dimension_b_drift.title: Call WF-50 (Stop Clarifier) uses mappingMode:passthrough in .md but pseudo Step 8 implies explicit field passing
dimension_b_drift.evidence: docs/pseudocode/WF-30.md line 39 — 'mappingMode:passthrough' for 'Call WF-50 (Stop Clarifier)'. docs/pseudocode/WF-30.pseudo:31-34 — Step 7 builds an explicit payload {phoneNumber, messageType, messageContent} and Step 8 says 'Call WF-50 (Stop Clarifier) with the prepared payload'. Passthrough mode will forward all fields from 'Build WF-50 (Stop Clarifier) Payload' Set node output — which does set exactly {phoneNumber, messageType, messageContent} — so runtime is correct. But the pseudo implies defineBelow-style explicit mapping, creating a minor documentation impression mismatch.
dimension_b_drift.recommended_action: Either update pseudo Step 8 to note 'passthrough forwards the Set node output' OR change .md node to use defineBelow to match the pseudo's intent. Functionally safe either way since the Set node output contains exactly the three required fields.

questions_for_human: The 'Call WF-50 (Stop Clarifier)' node uses mappingMode:passthrough (not defineBelow). This is functionally equivalent because the preceding 'Build WF-50 (Stop Clarifier) Payload' Set node emits exactly {phoneNumber, messageType, messageContent}. However if a future node is inserted between them that adds extra fields, passthrough would forward those extras to WF-50. Intentional design choice (passthrough for brevity) or should this be defineBelow for defensiveness, matching the Send Payment Reminder via WF-50 pattern?
